title: intentfirst.ai
summary: intentfirst.ai is a design-language framework — Context Grammar — giving AI systems the vocabulary to understand intent, not just input. Defines 8 Context Tokens and a 3-layer memory model, demonstrated across three applied projects.
thesis: AI knows what you asked. It doesn't know what you need — a shared vocabulary for context, not just intent, can let AI systems understand what a person actually needs in the moment.
experiment: Defined Context Grammar: 8 structured Context Tokens (Physical State, Cognitive Load, Social Exposure, Priority Weight, Form Factor, Feasibility, Autonomy Dial, Disclosure Dial) plus a 3-layer memory model (Identity / Accumulated Learning / Right Now), demonstrated across 3 applied projects — The Living Home, The Family Trip, Fluid Handoff.
question: Can a structured vocabulary for a user's physical state, cognitive load, and autonomy preference give AI/OS platforms a practical way to design for intent rather than literal input?

mine: Defined the Context Grammar framework: 8 structured Context Tokens describing who a user is in the moment, not just what they said
Designed the 3-layer memory model — Identity, Accumulated Learning, Right Now
Built 3 applied demonstration projects: The Living Home, The Family Trip, Fluid Handoff
Published the framework and site at intentfirst.ai
